outcome.technical: WHAT CHANGED, BY FILE, AND WHY IT IS HERE. (1) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py, the task's subject: BASE_CLAIM_SUFFIX and claim_launch's O_EXCL file are removed. claim_launch(ctx, name) is _locks.acquire(project, 'base-<phase>.<task>.<launch>', wait=0, per_call=True, reclaim=True), refusing with the library's own lines. base_run takes the claim, reads the mark again under it (new measure_launch: refuses a replaced launch or one that already ran), and gives the claim back in `finally` (release_launch), adding a WARNING if the release is refused because it was taken over. base_lock_name derives the name from the record's basename. drop_progress(ctx, path) also releases the launch's lock through _locks.release, which refuses a claim recording another process that still runs. (2) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_locks.py, where the note puts the primitive: BASE_PREFIX, a `base-<ascii id>` name shape in is_plugin_name/name_refusal, and acquire(reclaim=True). reclaim takes over a claim judge() reads as not live, in the call that judged it, through the stamped _take_over, and refuses a live one as the default does. (3) plugins/audit/scripts/usage/audit-usage.py, from note 3: acquire_lock's E_STALE-then-takeover=True retake is now one acquire(..., reclaim=True). Its docstring was corrected: it claimed the two-step refused a run that took the name in between, but the second call judged again and took over whatever it found. (4) tests/test_drive_phase.py: the new lc-block (lc1-lc7). Each case uses a real child process running base_run that either dies with os._exit after the claim and before `ran`, or holds until released. The block also has an AST scan of drive-phase.py's source (hand_rolled_claims) and its twin. bi13 now runs in a git-initialised world (_bk_world), because a lock lives in the clone's git dir. (5) tests/test__locks.py: the new rc-block, rc1-rc4: reclaim against a gone holder (twin: the default still answers E_STALE), a live holder, an unreadable claim young and aged, and base- name validity, with user-base-* refused. (6) tests/test_audit_usage.py: ur1. It wraps _locks.acquire and _locks.judge for one acquire_lock call and plants a live winner in each window: after an acquire answers E_STALE, and after judge reads the holder dead inside the retaking call. The winner must never be displaced. (7) tests/test__output_lints.py: lk4 read every caller of `_locks.acquire(` as text and flagged any line holding `isinstance(` and `code`. Once the driver called acquire, that flagged six unrelated driver lines, so the scan now reads the AST through _acquire_misreads: names bound to an acquire(...) result that are then tested with isinstance. lk4b is its twin. (8) PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: the drive-phase section's claim paragraph now describes the _locks claim, its takeover and the lc cases. (9) SECURITY.md, plugins/audit/commands/worktree.md and plugins/audit/scripts/governance/audit-lock.py (docstring only): each lists the plugin's lock names, and base-<id> is now one. (10) plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md: 'Every lock this script can take' became 'Every lock you take', because audit-lock.py now accepts base-<id>, which the list does not name. I did not add a paragraph because the file is at its measure-context ceiling: 61987 / 62000 now, under `measure-context.py --gate` exit 0. LIVENESS IS THE LIBRARY'S: _locks.liveness/judge decide; a refused ps reads 'unverified' and counts as live; an unparseable claim counts as live until STALE_MINUTES; an empty claim is taken over at once. No other hand-rolled exclusion exists in the P161 diff: base_running reads _locks.pid_alive, which is a liveness read, not an exclusion. DEPENDANTS: drive-without-model.py hook, _worktrees.py, test__filed_returns, test__invariants, test__worktrees, test_audit_status, test_commit_task_work and test_detect_plan_skip import the driver, and none calls drop_progress or claim_launch (git grep finds callers only in drive-phase.py and its suite). They are unchanged and their sweep is green. test_drive_phase.py's path dependants (sweep-costs.json, ci.yml, affected.py, reach-diff.py, test__runner_output, test_run_test_gate, test_stamp_verification) are unchanged in meaning. lc-block is a new staged block with no recorded cost, which the sweep weighs by the suite's figure over its blocks. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's dependants (_doctor_hygiene.py, test__deps and the eval/basename readers) are green; test__doctor_hygiene and test__deps both pass. HOW EDITS WERE MADE: early shell-heredoc edits to audit-lock.py, SECURITY.md and worktree.md drew a bash-write-guard notice. I restored those three files with git checkout (the diff was only mine, checked by --stat) and redid them with Edit, which the plan gate allowed. Later _locks.py edits were shell-written after an allowed Edit on that file. Every file is inside the widened scope.
outcome.descriptive: The base-run claim is a _locks lock: a killed holder is taken over by the next base-run and the base is measured, a live holder still refuses, and the driver's source is scanned so that it makes no exclusive file of its own. The usage backfill's retake is one reclaiming acquire, so it no longer displaces a run that won the lock in between.

lc2: a live child holding the claim makes the second base-run refuse with E_USAGE, naming its pid and measuring nothing; the child then answers E_OK
lc3: an unparseable claim is refused while young, and taken over and measured once aged past _locks.STALE_MINUTES
lc4: an empty claim is taken over at once and measured
lc5/lc6: an AST scan of drive-phase.py finds no O_EXCL, link, mkdir, exclusive open or .claim/.lock literal; its twin names a planted O_EXCL claim and stays quiet on _locks.acquire
